51:  * The element an input event belongs to: the nearest element (self or ancestor)
52:  * that has a `data-pathland-id` AND a `data-event-listeners` mask including `bit`.
53:  * Unlike {@link nodeOf} (which returns the deepest id-bearing element), this walks
54:  * up so a gesture declared on a container (e.g. a tap on a `VStack` row whose child
55:  * `Text` is what's actually clicked) is attributed to the node that listens — the
56:  * contract the GTK renderer follows (gesture attached to any widget with the bits).
57:  * Elements that declare no listeners are skipped, so non-listening children never
58:  * steal an event from a listening ancestor.

60: function eventNodeOf(target: Element | null, bit: number): HTMLElement | null {
61:   let el: Element | null = target;

272:               col += 1;
273:             }
274:             row += 1;
275:             col = 0;
276:           } else {
277:             if (col >= columns) {
278:               row += 1;
279:               col = 0;
280:             }
281:             setShell(c, row, col);
282:             col += 1;
283:           }
284:         }
285:       }
286:     }
287:   }
288:   // Phase 2: cross-axis FILL children in a stack stretch via align-self.
289:   for (const el of els) {
290:     const parent = el.parentElement;
291:     if (!parent) {
292:       continue;
293:     }
294:     const parentComp = componentByNode.get(parent) ?? 0;
295:     const mainH = STACK_MAIN_HORIZONTAL.has(parentComp);
296:     if (!STACK_MAIN_HORIZONTAL.has(parentComp) && !STACK_MAIN_VERTICAL.has(parentComp)) {
297:       continue;
298:     }
299:     if (fillsAxis(el, !mainH, false)) {
300:       el.style.alignSelf = "stretch";
301:     }
302:   }
303: }

305: /** The last `ROLE` code applied per element (morphing needs both role and text
306:  *  style to resolve the effective tag). */
307: const roleByNode = new WeakMap<HTMLElement, number>();

309: /** The retained `node id → DOM Node` registry the renderer works against. */
310: export interface DomRenderer {
311:   byId: Map<number, Node>;
312:   /**
313:    * Optional hook invoked when a slot's `ROUTE` property changes — the host wires it
314:    * to `history.pushState` so the browser URL mirrors the app's navigation (spec
315:    * DSL.md §4.5). Not called on hydrate (the URL is already correct).
316:    */
317:   onRoute?: (path: string) => void;
318:   /**
319:    * Optional hook invoked when the renderer's default back button (a
320:    * `PlatformDefault` nav slot at depth > 1) is clicked — the host wires it to a
321:    * `NAVIGATE` event with no URL, so the app pops its own back-stack (spec DSL.md
322:    * §4.5). Null/absent when the slot is `Custom` chrome or at depth 1.
323:    */
324:   onNavigateBack?: () => void;
325:   /** Optional design-token sink (defaults to document-root CSS variables). */
326:   tokenSink?: DesignTokenSink;
327:   /**
328:    * Optional media-event sink: the host wires it to `transport.send` so a bound
329:    * `AUDIO`/`VIDEO` node can report play/pause/time/ended/volume (host → guest).
330:    */
331:   onMediaEvent?: (batch: Uint8Array) => void;
332:   /**
333:    * Optional fit-event sink: the host wires it to `transport.send` so a
334:    * `SIZE_THAT_FITS` slot can report its derived fit index (`FIT_CHANGED`).
335:    */
336:   onFitEvent?: (batch: Uint8Array) => void;
337: }

339: /** Apply every opcode in a batch to the DOM (TREE structure + PARAMETER/META deltas). */
340: export function applyBatch(batch: Batch, renderer: DomRenderer): void {
341:   // SSR snapshot fit slots (`data-pathland-fit-cands`) touched by a structural
342:   // removal in this batch. The gate is torn down AFTER the whole batch, gated on
343:   // the slot's FINAL state (issue #141): a removal that does NOT reduce the slot
344:   // to a single live candidate (e.g. a band-crossing fit swap dropping a child
345:   // inside a candidate) must leave the gate intact — unwrapping it eagerly would
346:   // expose every candidate (the "all branches rendered" bug).
347:   const touchedFitGates = new Set<HTMLElement>();
348:   for (let i = 0; i < batch.opcodes.length; i++) {
349:     const op = batch.opcodes[i]!;
350:     try {
351:       switch (op.category) {
352:         case CAT_TREE:
353:           applyTree(op, renderer, touchedFitGates);
354:           break;
355:         case CAT_PARAMETER:
356:           applyStyle(op, batch.strings, renderer);
357:           break;
358:         case CAT_META:
359:           applyMeta(op, renderer);
360:           break;
361:         default:
362:           break;
363:       }
364:     } catch (err) {
365:       // The batch is a renderer-consuming instruction stream; an empty catch
366:       // would hide a structural bug. Log the exact op for remote diagnosis,
367:       // then rethrow (the host's handleMessage surfaces it).
368:       const el = renderer.byId.get(op.a);
369:       const where = el instanceof Element
370:         ? `${el.tagName.toLowerCase()}#${el.getAttribute("data-pathland-id")}.${el.className}`
371:         : String(el);
372:       console.error(
373:         `[pathland] applyBatch failed at op ${i}/${batch.opcodes.length} ` +
374:         `cat=${op.category} cmd=${op.command} a=${op.a} b=${op.b} c=${op.c} target=${where}`, err);
375:       throw err;
376:     }
377:   }
378:   for (const slot of touchedFitGates) {
379:     reconcileFitGate(slot);
380:   }
381:   // Derived layout (fill propagation, ZStack sizing/positioning, cross-axis
382:   // align-self) — mirrors the Rust SSR renderer's whole-tree decisions.
383:   applyLayout(renderer);
384: }

386: function applyMeta(op: Opcode, r: DomRenderer): void {
387:   switch (op.command) {
388:     case CMD_RESET: {
389:       for (const el of Array.from(r.byId.values())) {
390:         if (el.parentNode) {
391:           el.parentNode.removeChild(el);
392:         }
393:       }
394:       r.byId.clear();
395:       break;
396:     }
397:     case CMD_ENVIRONMENT:
398:     default:
399:       break;
400:   }
401: }

403: /** The node actually inserted into a parent's container: ZStack children are
404:  *  wrapped in a `grid-area:1/1` cell shell, grid cells (a GRID's bare children
405:  *  or a GRID_ROW's children) in an auto-placed cell shell (the layout pass sets
406:  *  their `justify-self`/`align-self` and explicit `grid-row`/`grid-column` from
407:  *  the container's structure/ALIGNMENT — mirrors the Rust SSR renderer), a
408:  *  GRID_ROW itself inserts directly (it is the row container, not a cell);
409:  *  everything else inserts directly. */
410: function placedChild(parent: Node, child: Node): Node {
411:   if (child instanceof HTMLElement) {
412:     const parentComp = componentByNode.get(parent);
413:     if (parentComp === COMPONENT_ZSTACK) {
414:       const wrapper = document.createElement("div");
415:       wrapper.style.gridArea = "1/1";
416:       wrapper.appendChild(child);
417:       return wrapper;
418:     }
419:     if (isGridComponent(parentComp) || parentComp === COMPONENT_GRID_ROW) {
420:       if (componentByNode.get(child) === COMPONENT_GRID_ROW) {
421:         return child; // a row container is a grid child, not a cell
422:       }
423:       const wrapper = document.createElement("div");
424:       wrapper.appendChild(child);
425:       return wrapper;
426:     }
427:   }
428:   return child;
429: }

431: /** Materialize a PICKER's child TEXT node as a native `<option>` (the Rust SSR
432:  *  renderer emits `<option data-pathland-id="{child}" value="{index}">` per
433:  *  child). The option keeps the child's id so its PARAMETER deltas resolve to it. */
434: function pickerOption(child: HTMLElement): HTMLElement {
435:   const opt = document.createElement("option");
436:   opt.textContent = child.textContent ?? "";
437:   const id = child.getAttribute("data-pathland-id");
438:   if (id) {
439:     opt.setAttribute("data-pathland-id", id);
440:   }
441:   return opt;
442: }

444: /** Keep a PICKER's option `value` attributes aligned with their index (the SSR
445:  *  renderer's `<option value="{i}">` scheme). */
446: function renumberPickerOptions(container: Node): void {
447:   if (!(container instanceof HTMLSelectElement)) {
448:     return;
449:   }
450:   Array.from(container.options).forEach((o, i) => {
451:     o.value = String(i);
452:   });
453: }

455: function applyTree(op: Opcode, r: DomRenderer, touchedFitGates: Set<HTMLElement>): void {
456:   // N→1 fit-slot reconcile (issue #141): the server's SSR snapshot carried EVERY
457:   // candidate behind CSS `@container` gated wrappers (`data-pathland-fit-cands`).
458:   // The downgrade to a single selected child is signalled by REMOVING a candidate
459:   // (a `REMOVE_CHILD`/`DELETE_NODE` on the slot). Record the touched slot and
460:   // reconcile it AFTER the batch (`reconcileFitGate`), once the REMOVE/DELETE
461:   // deltas have applied: only a slot that actually ended up with a single live
462:   // candidate is the downgrade — a removal that merely drops a child inside a
463:   // candidate (a band-crossing fit swap) must leave the gate intact. An
464:   // `INSERT_CHILD`/`CREATE_NODE` is never the downgrade: a `META::RESYNC` replays
465:   // the whole tree and the SSR gate must SURVIVE it (the CSS band keeps showing the
466:   // width-correct candidate).
467:   if (op.command === CMD_REMOVE_CHILD || op.command === CMD_DELETE_NODE) {
468:     const slot = nearestGatedFitSlot(op, r);
469:     if (slot) {
470:       touchedFitGates.add(slot);
471:     }
472:   }
473:   switch (op.command) {
474:     case CMD_CREATE_NODE: {
475:       // Hydration-aware: an id already present in the registry is the SSR-hydrated
476:       // element — reuse it (a resync/full snapshot replays CREATE for every node
477:       // without clobbering the visible DOM). Only create a fresh shell when absent.
478:       let el = r.byId.get(op.a);
479:       if (!el) {
480:         el = createElement(op.b);
481:         if (el.nodeType === Node.ELEMENT_NODE) {
482:           (el as HTMLElement).setAttribute("data-pathland-id", String(op.a));
483:         }
484:         r.byId.set(op.a, el);
485:       }
486:       if (el.nodeType === Node.ELEMENT_NODE) {
487:         componentByNode.set(el, op.b);
488:       }
489:       break;
490:     }
491:     case CMD_DELETE_NODE: {
492:       const el = r.byId.get(op.a);
493:       if (el) {
494:         const host = el as HTMLElement;
495:         // `DELETE_NODE` covers the whole subtree: every descendant's registry
496:         // entry must die too, or a later op could reuse a still-registered
497:         // (detached) element and double-parent it (HierarchyRequestError).
498:         purgeSubtreeRegistry(host, r);
499:         if (host.parentNode) {
500:           host.parentNode.removeChild(host);
501:         }
502:       }
503:       r.byId.delete(op.a);
504:       break;
505:     }
506:     case CMD_INSERT_CHILD: {
507:       const child = r.byId.get(op.b);
508:       const parentNode = r.byId.get(op.a);
509:       if (!child || !parentNode) {
510:         break;
511:       }
512:       let parent: Node = parentNode;
513:       // A media node gaining custom control children morphs its bare media
514:       // element into a `.pathland-media` wrapper (the Rust SSR emits the same
515:       // structure); the children then attach to the wrapper.
516:       const comp = componentByNode.get(parentNode);
517:       if ((comp === COMPONENT_AUDIO || comp === COMPONENT_VIDEO)
518:           && parentNode instanceof HTMLElement && parentNode.matches("audio,video")) {
519:         parent = mediaToWrapper(parentNode, r);
520:       }
521:       const container = childrenContainer(parent);
522:       // Hydration/idempotent-replay guard: skip when the child is already there
523:       // (the SSR DOM already holds the initial tree; a resync replays it), or
524:       // when a duplicate of the node already exists by id (drift protection —
525:       // never render a second copy the app did not emit).
526:       if (container && !container.contains(child)
527:           && !(child instanceof Element && container instanceof Element
528:             && container.querySelector(`[data-pathland-id="${op.b}"]`))) {
529:         let placed = placedChild(parent, child);
530:         if (comp === COMPONENT_PICKER && child instanceof HTMLElement) {
531:           // Picker children are option labels → materialize native `<option>`s.
532:           placed = pickerOption(child);
533:           r.byId.set(op.b, placed);
534:           componentByNode.set(placed, COMPONENT_TEXT);
535:         }
536:         insertAt(container, placed, op.c);
537:         if (comp === COMPONENT_PICKER) {
538:           renumberPickerOptions(container);
539:         }
540:         maybeAnimateInsert(parent, placed);
541:       }
542:       break;
543:     }
544:     case CMD_REMOVE_CHILD: {
545:       const child = r.byId.get(op.b);
546:       if (child && child.parentNode) {
547:         child.parentNode.removeChild(child);
548:       }
549:       break;
550:     }
551:     case CMD_MOVE_CHILD: {
552:       const child = r.byId.get(op.b);
553:       if (!child) {
554:         break;
555:       }
556:       const parent = r.byId.get(op.a);
557:       if (parent) {
558:         const container = childrenContainer(parent);
559:         if (container) {
560:           // Detach the child (and its now-empty ZStack wrapper, if any) so the
561:           // wrapper-count stays in sync with the Rust SSR structure.
562:           const oldParent = child.parentNode;
563:           child.parentNode?.removeChild(child);
564:           if (
565:             oldParent instanceof HTMLElement &&
566:             oldParent !== container &&
567:             oldParent.childElementCount === 0 &&
568:             oldParent.style.position === "absolute"
569:           ) {
570:             oldParent.remove();
571:           }
572:           let placed = placedChild(parent, child);
573:           if (componentByNode.get(parent) === COMPONENT_PICKER && child instanceof HTMLElement) {
574:             placed = pickerOption(child);
575:             r.byId.set(op.b, placed);
576:             componentByNode.set(placed, COMPONENT_TEXT);
577:           }
578:           insertAt(container, placed, op.c);
579:           if (componentByNode.get(parent) === COMPONENT_PICKER) {
580:             renumberPickerOptions(container);
581:           }
582:         }
583:       }
584:       break;
585:     }
586:     default:
587:       break;
588:   }
589: }

591: function insertAt(container: Node, child: Node, index: number): void {
592:   // Inserting a node into itself or its own subtree yields an incorrect node
593:   // tree — the child is effectively already positioned; skip (never throw).
594:   if (child === container || container.contains(child)) {
595:     return;
596:   }
597:   // The protocol's INSERT/MOVE index counts ELEMENT children. Debug-comment
598:   // nodes (`<!-- #id … -->`, `pathland.debug-html=true`) are sibling children
599:   // in the SSR-hydrated DOM, so counting them in `visible` shifts every index
600:   // and e.g. would insert a trailing sidebar BEFORE the main area. Count
601:   // elements only; the injected nav-back button is excluded by class.
602:   const visible = Array.from(container.childNodes).filter(
603:     (n) =>
604:       n.nodeType === Node.ELEMENT_NODE &&
605:       !(n instanceof HTMLElement && n.classList.contains(NAV_BACK_CLASS)),
606:   );
607:   const target = visible[index];
608:   detachIfWrongParent(container, child);
609:   if (target) {
610:     if (target === child || target.contains(child)) {
611:       // Would yield an incorrect node tree (inserting a node before itself or a
612:       // descendant) — the child is already positioned; nothing to do.
613:       return;
614:     }
615:     container.insertBefore(child, target);
616:   } else {
617:     container.appendChild(child);
618:   }
619: }

621: // --- renderer-provided navigation chrome (spec DSL.md §4.5) ---
622: // A `PlatformDefault` nav slot at depth > 1 gets a default back button drawn by
623: // the DOM renderer (the web has no native navigation container). The button is
624: // a tracked child of the slot that the reconcile ignores (see `insertAt`), so
625: // TREE deltas never displace it. `Custom` chrome slots never get one.
626: 
627: /** The injected default back button's class (excluded from child indexing). */
628: export const NAV_BACK_CLASS = "pathland-nav-back";
629: 
630: /** Whether an element is a nav slot (carries a `data-pathland-route`). */
631: function isNavSlot(el: HTMLElement): boolean {
632:   return el.hasAttribute("data-pathland-route");
633: }
634: 
635: /** The slot's chrome mode: `true` when the developer owns all nav UI. */
636: function isCustomChrome(el: HTMLElement): boolean {
637:   return el.getAttribute("data-pathland-nav-chrome") === "custom";
638: }
639: 
640: /** The slot's current depth (defaults to 1 = root destination). */
641: function slotDepth(el: HTMLElement): number {
642:   return Math.max(1, Number(el.getAttribute("data-pathland-depth") ?? "1") || 1);
643: }
644: 
645: /** The injected back button inside a slot, if present. */
646: function injectedBackButton(el: HTMLElement): HTMLButtonElement | null {
647:   return el.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>(`.${NAV_BACK_CLASS}`);
648: }
649: 
650: /**
651:  * Reconcile the renderer's default back button for a nav slot: shown for a
652:  * `PlatformDefault` slot at depth > 1, removed for `Custom` chrome or depth 1.
653:  * Called from `SET_PROPERTY` (depth/chrome changes) and once at hydrate.
654:  */
655: export function updateNavBackButton(el: HTMLElement, r: DomRenderer): void {
656:   if (!isNavSlot(el) || isCustomChrome(el) || slotDepth(el) <= 1) {
657:     injectedBackButton(el)?.remove();
658:     return;
659:   }
660:   let back = injectedBackButton(el);
661:   if (!back) {
662:     back = document.createElement("button");
663:     back.type = "button";
664:     back.className = NAV_BACK_CLASS;
665:     back.setAttribute("aria-label", "Back");
666:     back.textContent = "‹ Back";
667:     back.addEventListener("click", () => r.onNavigateBack?.());
668:     el.insertBefore(back, el.firstChild); // above the destination
669:   }
670: }
671: 
672: /** Reconcile the default back button for every nav slot in the tree (hydrate). */
673: export function updateNavBackButtons(r: DomRenderer): void {
674:   for (const node of r.byId.values()) {
675:     if (node instanceof HTMLElement && isNavSlot(node)) {
676:       updateNavBackButton(node, r);
677:     }
678:   }
679: }

681: // --- swap transitions (spec DSL.md §4.5 / MODIFIERS.md TRANSITION) ---
682: // When a child is inserted into a slot carrying a `data-pathland-transition` hint,
683: // the DOM client animates the new subtree in (fade/slide/scale). This is a pure
684: // renderer-side animation of its own output cache — never app state.
685: 
686: const TRANSITION_KEYFRAMES: Record<string, string> = {
687:   platform: "@keyframes pl-platform { from { opacity: 0; } to { opacity: 1; } }",
688:   fade: "@keyframes pl-fade { from { opacity: 0; } to { opacity: 1; } }",
689:   slide:
690:     "@keyframes pl-slide { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateX(16px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } }",
691:   scale:
692:     "@keyframes pl-scale { from { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.96); } to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } }",
693: };
694: 
695: let transitionsInjected = false;
696: 
697: function ensureTransitionStyles(): void {
698:   if (transitionsInjected || typeof document === "undefined") {
699:     return;
700:   }
701:   transitionsInjected = true;
702:   const style = document.createElement("style");
703:   style.setAttribute("data-pathland-transitions", "");
704:   style.textContent = Object.values(TRANSITION_KEYFRAMES).join("\n");
705:   document.head.appendChild(style);
706: }
707: 
708: function maybeAnimateInsert(parent: Node, child: Node): void {
709:   if (!(parent instanceof HTMLElement) || !(child instanceof HTMLElement)) {
710:     return;
711:   }
712:   const name = parent.getAttribute("data-pathland-transition");
713:   if (!name) {
714:     return;
715:   }
716:   ensureTransitionStyles();
717:   const key = TRANSITION_KEYFRAMES[name] ? name : "platform";
718:   child.style.animation = `pl-${key} 180ms ease-out`;
719:   child.addEventListener("animationend", () => {
720:     child.style.animation = "";
721:   }, { once: true });
722: }

724: /** Resolve an element's role shell kind: from the component when known (fresh
725:  *  nodes), else from its tag (SSR-hydrated nodes have no component). */
726: function shellKind(el: HTMLElement): "generic" | "native" | "other" {
727:   const comp = componentByNode.get(el);
728:   if (comp !== undefined) {
729:     if (GENERIC_COMPONENTS.includes(comp)) {
730:       return "generic";
731:     }
732:     if (NATIVE_ROLE_COMPONENTS.includes(comp)) {
733:       return "native";
734:     }
735:     return "other";
736:   }
737:   const t = el.tagName.toLowerCase();
738:   if (t === "div" || t === "span") {
739:     return el.classList.contains("pathland-menu") || el.classList.contains("pathland-stepper")
740:       ? "other"
741:       : "generic";
742:   }
743:   if (
744:     t === "button" ||
745:     t === "input" ||
746:     t === "label" ||
747:     t === "select" ||
748:     t === "textarea" ||
749:     t === "progress" ||
750:     t === "img"
751:   ) {
752:     return "native";
753:   }
754:   return "other";
755: }

757: /** Replace an element with one of a different tag (a semantic role retag),
758:  *  preserving attributes, children, and the registry entry. */
759: function morphRole(el: HTMLElement, tag: string, r: DomRenderer): HTMLElement {
760:   const fresh = document.createElement(tag);
761:   for (const attr of Array.from(el.attributes)) {
762:     fresh.setAttribute(attr.name, attr.value);
763:   }
764:   while (el.firstChild) {
765:     fresh.appendChild(el.firstChild);
766:   }
767:   if (el.parentNode) {
768:     el.parentNode.replaceChild(fresh, el);
769:   }
770:   const id = Number(el.getAttribute("data-pathland-id"));
771:   if (id) {
772:     r.byId.set(id, fresh);
773:   }
774:   const comp = componentByNode.get(el);
775:   if (comp !== undefined) {
776:     componentByNode.set(fresh, comp);
777:   }
778:   const role = roleByNode.get(el);
779:   if (role !== undefined) {
780:     roleByNode.set(fresh, role);
781:   }
782:   copyTypography(el, fresh);
783:   return fresh;
784: }

786: /** Resolve and apply the semantic tag + ARIA role for an element from its
787:  *  current `ROLE` / `TEXT_STYLE` state (a heading `TEXT_STYLE` always wins).
788:  *  Retags a generic shell in place when the effective tag differs. */
789: function applySemantic(el: HTMLElement, r: DomRenderer): void {
790:   const kind = shellKind(el);
791:   const role = roleByNode.get(el) ?? 0;
792:   const style = textStyleByNode.get(el);
793:   const tag = textTag(kind, role, style ?? null);
794:   let current = el;
795:   if (tag && current.tagName.toLowerCase() !== tag) {
796:     current = morphRole(current, tag, r);
797:   }
798:   const aria = ariaRole(kind, role);
799:   if (aria) {
800:     current.setAttribute("role", aria);
801:   } else {
802:     current.removeAttribute("role");
803:   }
804: }

806: function applyStyle(op: Opcode, strings: Uint8Array, r: DomRenderer): void {
807:   if (op.command === CMD_SET_DESIGN_TOKEN) {
808:     applyDesignToken(op, strings, r.tokenSink ?? createTokenSink());
809:     return;
810:   }
811:   const node = r.byId.get(op.a);
812:   if (!node || node.nodeType !== Node.ELEMENT_NODE) {
813:     return;
814:   }
815:   const el = node as HTMLElement;
816:   switch (op.command) {
817:     case CMD_SET_TEXT:
818:       setNodeText(el, readString(strings, op.b));
819:       break;
820:     case CMD_SET_DATE: {
821:       const input = el.matches("input[type=date],input[type=time],input[type=datetime-local]")
822:         ? (el as HTMLInputElement)
823:         : el.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("input[type=date],input[type=time],input[type=datetime-local]");
824:       if (input) {
825:         if (input.type === "time") {
826:           input.value = millisToTime(op.c);
827:         } else if (input.type === "datetime-local") {
828:           const date = daysToIso(op.b);

830:           input.value = date ? `${date}T${time}` : time;

835:       break;
836:     }

838:       const propId = op.b & 0xffff;
839:       const valueType = (op.b >>> 16) & 0xff;
840:       if (valueType === VAL_STRING) {

846:           applyStringProperty(el, propId, text);
847:           if (propId === PROP_AUDIO_SOURCE || propId === PROP_VIDEO_SOURCE) {

849:             // (a control-less media node renders native controls), and resume
850:             // playback if the app was playing (a src change pauses the element).
851:             ensureMediaElement(el, propId);
852:             applyStringProperty(el, propId, text);
853:             setupMediaElement(el, r);
854:             finalizeNativeMedia(el);
855:             resumeIfPlaying(el);
856:           }
857:         }
858:       } else if (valueType === VAL_DESIGN_TOKEN) {
859:         applyTokenRefProperty(el, propId, readString(strings, op.c));
860:       } else if (valueType === VAL_LIST) {
861:         applyFitQuery(el, r, readList(strings, op.c));

867:         // a generic shell is retagged to its semantic element; the ARIA `role`
868:         // attribute is set only when the element does not already convey it.
869:         roleByNode.set(el, Math.round(f32FromBits(op.c)) & 0xff);

873:         // (`<h1>`–`<h5>`) — always, even without `ROLE_HEADER`; raw font
874:         // modifiers never imply a heading. Absence is "no style" (the enum has
875:         // no NONE — LARGE_TITLE is code 0, a real heading style). The style also
876:         // sets its default size/weight, unless an explicit FONT_SIZE/FONT_WEIGHT

878:         applyTextStyle(el, Math.round(f32FromBits(op.c)) & 0xff);

889:         } else {
890:           el.removeAttribute("data-pathland-nav-chrome");
891:         }

897:         applyNumericProperty(el, propId, valueType, op.c);

900:     }
901:     default:
902:       break;
903:   }
904: }

906: /** Set a node's text, honoring text fields/editors and label spans (SSR structure). */

908:   const input = el.querySelector("input[type=text],input[type=password]");

936: /** Set an icon's accessibility: a `LABEL` makes it presentable
937:  *  (`role="img"` + `aria-label`); without one it is decorative (`aria-hidden`). */
938: function syncIconAria(el: Element, label?: string): void {

952: function applyStringProperty(el: HTMLElement, propId: number, text: string): void {
953:   switch (propId) {
954:     case PROP_TEXT:
955:     case PROP_LABEL: {
956:       // On a media element the accessibility label is the `alt` text (mirrors
957:       // the Rust SSR renderer); on a semantic icon it makes the svg presentable;
958:       // elsewhere it's the caption/label span.
959:       const icon = el.matches("svg.pathland-icon")
960:         ? el
961:         : el.querySelector("svg.pathland-icon");
962:       const media = el.matches("img,audio,video") ? el : null;
963:       if (media) {
964:         media.setAttribute("alt", text);

966:         syncIconAria(icon, text);
967:       } else {
968:         const span = el.querySelector(".pathland-label");
969:         if (span) {
970:           span.textContent = text;
971:         } else {
972:           setNodeText(el, text);
973:         }
974:       }
975:       break;
976:     }
977:     case PROP_ICON_NAME: {
978:       // A semantic icon: swap the filled inner markup for the canonical name.
979:       // The glyph comes from an embedded sibling / the memo cache / a lazy
980:       // fetch of the renderer-owned `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` (icons.ts).
981:       const svg = el.matches("svg.pathland-icon")
982:         ? el
983:         : el.querySelector("svg.pathland-icon");
984:       if (svg) {
985:         setIcon(svg, text);
986:       }
987:       break;
988:     }
989:     case PROP_PROMPT: {
990:       const input = el.querySelector("input[type=text]");
991:       if (input instanceof HTMLInputElement) {
992:         input.placeholder = text;
993:       }
994:       break;
995:     }
996:     case PROP_IMAGE_SOURCE: {
997:       const img = el.matches("img") ? el : el.querySelector("img");
998:       if (img instanceof HTMLImageElement) {
999:         img.src = text;
1000:       }
1001:       break;
1002:     }
1003:     case PROP_AUDIO_SOURCE: {
1004:       const audio = el.matches("audio") ? el : el.querySelector("audio");
1005:       if (audio instanceof HTMLAudioElement) {
1006:         audio.src = text;
1007:       }
1008:       break;
1009:     }
1010:     case PROP_VIDEO_SOURCE: {
1011:       const video = el.matches("video") ? el : el.querySelector("video");
1012:       if (video instanceof HTMLVideoElement) {
1013:         video.src = text;
1014:       }
1015:       break;
1016:     }
1017:     case PROP_FONT_FAMILY: {
1018:       el.style.fontFamily = text;
1019:       break;
1020:     }
1021:     case PROP_GRID_TRACKS: {
1022:       // A grid's per-track spec (spec §grid model): `flex`/`fixed:<pts>`/
1023:       // `adaptive:<pts>` comma-separated → the CSS track template; takes
1024:       // precedence over the count (the DSL emits one or the other).
1025:       const comp = componentByNode.get(el);
1026:       const isH = comp === COMPONENT_LAZY_HGRID;
1027:       const tracks = text.split(",").map((t) => t.trim());
1028:       const css = tracks
1029:         .map((t) => {
1030:           if (t.startsWith("fixed:")) return `${t.slice("fixed:".length)}px`;
1031:           if (t.startsWith("adaptive:")) return `minmax(${t.slice("adaptive:".length)}px,1fr)`;

1037:       } else {
1038:         el.style.gridTemplateColumns = css;

1041:     }

1043:       break;
1044:   }

1047: function applyNumericProperty(el: HTMLElement, propId: number, valueType: number, bits: number): void {
1048:   switch (propId) {
1049:     case PROP_SELECTED: {
1050:       const input = el.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("input[type=checkbox]");
1051:       if (input) {
1052:         const on = (valueType === 0x01 ? bits & 0xff : bits) !== 0;
1053:         input.checked = on;
1054:         // Button-style toggles are rendered with `role=checkbox` + `aria-pressed`
1055:         // (the Rust SSR renderer's TOGGLE_STYLE=Button); switch/checkbox styles
1056:         // carry only the native `checked` state.
1057:         if (input.getAttribute("role") === "checkbox") {
1058:           input.setAttribute("aria-pressed", on ? "true" : "false");
1059:         }
1060:       }
1061:       break;
1062:     }
1063:     case PROP_VALUE: {
1064:       const range = el.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("input[type=range]");
1065:       // In-flight interaction (spec EVENTS.md): while the user is dragging the
1066:       // slider, its thumb is user-authoritative — a server echo of VALUE must
1067:       // not fight the pointer (flicker).
1068:       if (range && !isRangeInFlight(range)) {
1069:         range.value = String(f32FromBits(bits));
1070:       }
1071:       const stepText = el.querySelector(".pathland-stepper span");
1072:       if (stepText) {
1073:         stepText.textContent = String(Math.round(f32FromBits(bits) * 100) / 100);
1074:       }
1075:       const gauge = el.matches(".pathland-gauge")
1076:         ? el
1077:         : el.querySelector<HTMLElement>(".pathland-gauge");
1078:       if (gauge) {
1079:         const max = Number(gauge.dataset.max ?? 1);
1080:         const min = Number(gauge.dataset.min ?? 0);
1081:         const span = max - min;
1082:         const pct = span <= 0 ? 0 : ((f32FromBits(bits) - min) / span) * 100;
1083:         const bar = gauge.firstElementChild;
1084:         if (bar instanceof HTMLElement) {
1085:           bar.style.width = pct + "%";
1086:         }
1087:       }
1088:       break;
1089:     }
1090:     case PROP_SELECTION: {
1091:       const select = el.matches("select")
1092:         ? (el as HTMLSelectElement)
1093:         : el.querySelector<HTMLSelectElement>("select");
1094:       if (select) {
1095:         // Index-based, matching the SSR `<option value="{index}">` scheme.
1096:         select.selectedIndex = bits;
1097:       }
1098:       break;
1099:     }
1100:     case PROP_COLOR_VALUE: {
1101:       const input = el.matches("input[type=color]")
1102:         ? el
1103:         : el.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("input[type=color]");
1104:       if (input instanceof HTMLInputElement) {
1105:         input.value = argbToHex(bits);
1106:       }
1107:       break;
1108:     }
1109:     case PROP_BINDING_ID: {
1110:       el.dataset.bindingId = String(bits >>> 0);
1111:       break;
1112:     }
1113:     case PROP_COLOR: {
1114:       // A COLOR / SHAPE node's COLOR property is its fill: it renders as a
1115:       // background (the generic handler below sets the text color, which the
1116:       // Rust SSR renderer also emits alongside the fill).
1117:       const comp = componentByNode.get(el);
1118:       if (comp === COMPONENT_COLOR || comp === COMPONENT_SHAPE) {
1119:         el.style.backgroundColor = argbToRgba(bits);
1120:       }
1121:       applyProperty(el, propId, valueType, bits);
1122:       break;
1123:     }
1124:     case PROP_ENABLED:
1125:       applyEnabled(el, bits);
1126:       break;
1127:     case PROP_ALIGNMENT: {
1128:       // ZStack/grids position on BOTH axes with a 2D code (spec §grid model /
1129:       // §ZStack); stacks/others use the single-axis cross `align-items` token.
1130:       const comp = componentByNode.get(el);
1131:       if (isGridComponent(comp) || comp === COMPONENT_ZSTACK) {
1132:         const code = valueType === VAL_ENUM ? bits & 0xff : Math.round(f32FromBits(bits));
1133:         el.style.justifyItems = alignHCss(code);
1134:         el.style.alignItems = alignVCss(code);
1135:       } else {
1136:         applyProperty(el, propId, valueType, bits);
1137:       }
1138:       break;
1139:     }
1140:     case PROP_GRID_COLUMNS: {
1141:       // A grid's column count (the fixed track of vertical grids): a positive
1142:       // count mirrors into `grid-template-columns` and NEVER into a pixel width
1143:       // (spec §grid model); FILL/absent = auto-fit (no template).
1144:       const comp = componentByNode.get(el);
1145:       const n = f32FromBits(bits);
1146:       if (comp !== COMPONENT_LAZY_HGRID && isGridComponent(comp)) {
1147:         el.style.gridTemplateColumns = n > 0 ? `repeat(${Math.round(n)},minmax(0,1fr))` : "";
1148:       }
1149:       break;
1150:     }
1151:     case PROP_GRID_ROWS: {
1152:       // A grid's row count (the `LAZY_HGRID` fixed track): a positive count
1153:       // mirrors into `grid-template-rows`; FILL/absent = auto-fit.
1154:       const comp = componentByNode.get(el);
1155:       const n = f32FromBits(bits);
1156:       if ((comp === COMPONENT_GRID || comp === COMPONENT_LAZY_HGRID) && isGridComponent(comp)) {
1157:         el.style.gridTemplateRows = n > 0 ? `repeat(${Math.round(n)},minmax(0,1fr))` : "";
1158:       }
1159:       break;
1160:     }
1161:     default:
1162:       applyProperty(el, propId, valueType, bits);
1163:       break;
1164:   }
1165: }

1167: /** Whether `comp` is a grid container (GRID / lazy grids). */
1168: function isGridComponent(comp: number | undefined): boolean {
1169:   return comp === COMPONENT_GRID || comp === COMPONENT_LAZY_VGRID || comp === COMPONENT_LAZY_HGRID;

1172: /**
1173:  * A ProgressView's indicator properties: morphs the element between the
1174:  * determinate `<progress>` and the indeterminate `pathland-spinner` div (the
1175:  * Rust renderer's SSR shapes) and applies the determinate value. Mirrors the
1176:  * Rust indeterminate rule: `IS_INDETERMINATE != 0 || PROGRESS < 0`.
1177:  */

1179:   const on = valueType === VAL_U8 ? bits & 0xff : bits;

1181:   const el2 = morphProgress(el, r, indeterminate);
1182:   if (propId === PROP_PROGRESS && el2 instanceof HTMLProgressElement) {
1183:     const value = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, f32FromBits(bits)));

1189: /** Replace a ProgressView element between its two shapes, preserving attributes and the byId entry. */

1191:   const isSpinner = el.classList.contains("pathland-spinner");
1192:   if (wantSpinner === isSpinner) {
1193:     return el;
1194:   }
1195:   const fresh = wantSpinner
1196:     ? (() => {
1197:         const s = document.createElement("div");
1198:         s.className = "pathland-spinner";
1199:         return s;
1200:       })()
1201:     : (() => {
1202:         const p = document.createElement("progress");
1203:         p.max = 1;
1204:         return p;
1205:       })();
1206:   for (const attr of Array.from(el.attributes)) {
1207:     // A spinner is a plain div — it carries no `max`/`value` (the Rust SSR
1208:     // renderer's `<div class="pathland-spinner">`).
1209:     if (wantSpinner && (attr.name === "max" || attr.name === "value")) {
1210:       continue;
1211:     }
1212:     fresh.setAttribute(attr.name, attr.value);
1213:   }
1214:   if (el.parentNode) {

1216:   }

1218:   if (id) {
1219:     r.byId.set(id, fresh);
1220:   }
1221:   componentByNode.set(fresh, COMPONENT_PROGRESS_VIEW);

1225: // --- media (app-driven AUDIO/VIDEO) ---

1227: /** Per-element media state: echo suppression windows + the last app-requested
1228:  *  playing state (so a source change can resume playback). */
1229: const mediaState = new WeakMap<HTMLMediaElement, {
1230:   suppressUntil: number;
1231:   suppressTimeUntil: number;
1232:   playing: boolean;
1233:   lastReported: number;
1234:   lastReportedVolume: number;
1235:   reportTimer: number;
1236: }>();

1238: /** The media element of a node: the element itself when it IS the media, else the
1239:  *  inner `<audio>`/`<video>` of a `.pathland-media` wrapper. */
1240: function mediaElementOf(el: HTMLElement): HTMLMediaElement | null {
1241:   return el.matches("audio,video")
1242:     ? (el as HTMLMediaElement)
1243:     : el.querySelector<HTMLMediaElement>("audio,video");
1244: }

1246: /** Ensure a media node's container holds an inner (hidden) media element,
1247:  *  creating it for a live-created custom-controls node that lacks one yet. */
1248: function ensureMediaElement(el: HTMLElement, propId: number): HTMLMediaElement | null {
1249:   if (el.matches("audio,video")) {
1250:     return el as HTMLMediaElement;
1251:   }
1252:   let media = el.querySelector<HTMLMediaElement>("audio,video");
1253:   if (!media) {
1254:     media = document.createElement(propId === PROP_VIDEO_SOURCE ? "video" : "audio");
1255:     media.setAttribute("data-pathland-media", "");
1256:     el.prepend(media);
1257:   }
1258:   return media;
1259: }

1261: /** The cadence for `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` reports — ~30/s (≈ every 33 ms of
1262:  *  playback progress). The DOM client samples the element's position on this
1263:  *  interval (the browser's `timeupdate` is only ~4 Hz), reporting whenever it
1264:  *  advances; evens out to ~30 reports/s while playing (spec/EVENTS.md Media —
1265:  *  parity with the GTK renderer's 30 Hz gate). Background tabs throttle timers
1266:  *  to ≥1 s, so this is best-effort when not visible/focused. */
1267: const TIME_UPDATE_MAX_INTERVAL_S = 1 / 30;
1268: const TIME_UPDATE_SAMPLE_MS = 33;
1269: 
1270: /** Attach a media node's element once: wire the app-driven media element to the
1271:  *  host's media-event sink (play/pause/time/ended/volume, spec/EVENTS.md). */
1272: export function setupMediaElement(el: HTMLElement, r: DomRenderer): void {
1273:   const media = mediaElementOf(el);
1274:   if (!media || mediaState.has(media)) {
1275:     return;
1276:   }
1277:   const state = { suppressUntil: 0, suppressTimeUntil: 0, playing: false, lastReported: 0, lastReportedVolume: -1, reportTimer: 0 };
1278:   mediaState.set(media, state);
1279:   const id = Number(el.getAttribute("data-pathland-id"));
1280:   const send = r.onMediaEvent;
1281:   if (!send) {
1282:     return;
1283:   }
1284:   // Play/pause/volume are reported only when the media has NATIVE controls —
1285:   // the only case a user drives them directly. App-driven custom-control media
1286:   // (a hidden element under app controls) never echoes them: every such change
1287:   // is app-initiated, so reporting it back would lock the player state.
1288:   if (media.controls) {
1289:     media.addEventListener("play", () => {
1290:       if (performance.now() >= state.suppressUntil) {
1291:         send(encodeMediaPlayStateChanged(id, true));
1292:       }
1293:     });
1294:     media.addEventListener("pause", () => {
1295:       if (performance.now() >= state.suppressUntil) {
1296:         send(encodeMediaPlayStateChanged(id, false));
1297:       }
1298:     });
1299:     media.addEventListener("volumechange", () => {
1300:       if (performance.now() >= state.suppressUntil) {
1301:         state.lastReportedVolume = media.volume;
1302:         send(encodeMediaVolumeChanged(id, media.volume));
1303:       }
1304:     });
1305:   }
1306:   // Time + ended are always reported: the app displays progress and advances on
1307:   // end. The DOM client SAMPLES the position every ~33 ms (the browser's native
1308:   // `timeupdate` is only ~4 Hz), reporting whenever it advances a cadence step
1309:   // (≈ 30 reports/s while playing; spec/EVENTS.md Media — parity with the GTK
1310:   // renderer's 30 Hz gate). The sampler stops when removed (CMD_DELETE_NODE).
1311:   state.reportTimer = window.setInterval(() => {
1312:     if (!media.paused
1313:         && performance.now() >= state.suppressTimeUntil
1314:         && Math.abs(media.currentTime - state.lastReported) >= TIME_UPDATE_MAX_INTERVAL_S) {
1315:       state.lastReported = media.currentTime;
1316:       send(encodeMediaTimeUpdated(id, media.currentTime));
1317:     }
1318:   }, TIME_UPDATE_SAMPLE_MS);
1319:   media.addEventListener("ended", () => {
1320:     send(encodeMediaEnded(id));
1321:   });
1322: }

1324: /** Test-only: set a media element's last-reported position (the echo-guard
1325:  *  basis for `MEDIA_POSITION` writes, spec/EVENTS.md Media). */
1326: export function __setMediaLastReported(el: HTMLMediaElement, seconds: number): void {
1327:   const state = mediaState.get(el);
1328:   if (state) {
1329:     state.lastReported = seconds;
1330:   }
1331: }

1333: // --- SizeThatFits (FIT_QUERY → local fit → FIT_CHANGED only on transitions) ---

1335: interface FitSlotState {
1336:   thresholds: number[];
1337:   lastIndex: number;
1338:   observer: ResizeObserver | null;
1339: }

1341: /** Per-`SIZE_THAT_FITS` slot state: the candidate thresholds + last reported index. */
1342: const fitState = new WeakMap<HTMLElement, FitSlotState>();
1343: 
1344: /** The fit rule (spec/PRIMITIVES.md): max i with thresholds[i] <= width;
1345:  *  thresholds ascending, equal thresholds pick the lower index (stable). */

12: export interface Batch {
13:   readonly version: number;
14:   readonly flags: number;
15:   /** Per-stream monotonic message sequence (guest → host delta batches; 0 for heartbeat/requests). */
16:   readonly sequence: number;
17:   readonly opcodes: Opcode[];
18:   readonly strings: Uint8Array;
19: }
20: 
21: /** A protocol-level decode failure (truncation, bad magic, unsupported version). */
22: export class ProtocolError extends Error {}
23: 
24: function dv(bytes: Uint8Array): DataView {
25:   return new DataView(bytes.buffer, bytes.byteOffset, bytes.byteLength);
26: }
27: 
28: /**
29:  * Parse a self-contained PLPL batch:
30:  * `[magic u32][version u16][flags u16][sequence u32][opcodeCount u32]`,
31:  * then `opcodeCount × 16-byte opcodes`, then `[stringsLen u32][strings…]`.
32:  * Every read is bounds-checked.
33:  */
34: export function parseBatch(bytes: Uint8Array): Batch {
35:   if (bytes.length < HEADER_SIZE) {
36:     throw new ProtocolError("batch truncated");
37:   }
38:   const view = dv(bytes);
39:   if (view.getUint32(0, true) !== MAGIC) {
40:     throw new ProtocolError("bad batch magic");
41:   }
42:   const version = view.getUint16(4, true);
43:   if (version !== VERSION) {
44:     throw new ProtocolError(`unsupported batch version ${version}`);
45:   }
46:   const flags = view.getUint16(6, true);
47:   const sequence = view.getUint32(8, true);
48:   const opcodeCount = view.getUint32(12, true);
49:   const opcodesEnd = HEADER_SIZE + opcodeCount * OPCODE_SIZE;
50:   if (opcodesEnd + 4 > bytes.length) {
51:     throw new ProtocolError("batch truncated (opcodes)");
52:   }
53:   const opcodes: Opcode[] = [];
54:   for (let i = 0; i < opcodeCount; i++) {
55:     const pos = HEADER_SIZE + i * OPCODE_SIZE;
56:     opcodes.push({
57:       category: view.getUint8(pos),
58:       command: view.getUint8(pos + 1),
59:       flags: view.getUint16(pos + 2, true),
60:       a: view.getUint32(pos + 4, true),
61:       b: view.getUint32(pos + 8, true),
62:       c: view.getUint32(pos + 12, true),
63:     });
64:   }
65:   const stringsLen = view.getUint32(opcodesEnd, true);
66:   const stringsStart = opcodesEnd + 4;
67:   if (stringsStart + stringsLen > bytes.length) {
68:     throw new ProtocolError("batch truncated (strings)");
69:   }
70:   return {
71:     version,
72:     flags,
73:     sequence,
74:     opcodes,
75:     strings: bytes.subarray(stringsStart, stringsStart + stringsLen),
76:   };
77: }

82:     throw new ProtocolError("string offset out of bounds");

84:   const view = dv(strings);

89:   }
90:   return new TextDecoder().decode(strings.subarray(start, start + len));

1: // WebSocket transport: connects to the server's reserved `/_pathland/ws`,
2: // applies each received PLPL batch to the DOM renderer, negotiates the protocol
3: // version, and reports raw-input events back. Reconnect/backoff, heartbeat, and
4: // sequence-gap recovery (lost batches without a disconnect → META::RESYNC) live
5: // here.
6: 
7: import type { Batch } from "./plpl";
8: import { ProtocolError, parseBatch } from "./plpl";
9: import { applyBatch, type DomRenderer } from "./apply";
10: import { encodePing, encodeResync } from "./events";
11: import { FLAG_HOST_TO_GUEST, VERSION } from "./constants";
12: import { log } from "./log";
13: import { describeBatch, describeBatchDetail } from "./describe";
14: 
15: export type TransportStatus = "connecting" | "open" | "reconnecting";
16: 
17: export interface TransportOptions {
18:   /** WebSocket URL, e.g. `ws://host/_pathland/ws`. */
19:   url: string;
20:   /** The retained-node registry deltas are applied to. */
21:   renderer: DomRenderer;
22:   /** Invoked after a batch is successfully applied. */
23:   onBatch?: (batch: Batch) => void;
24:   onStatus?: (status: TransportStatus) => void;
25:   /**
26:    * Invoked on every socket open (first connect and reconnect), before any RESYNC —
27:    * the DOM client sends its `META::ENVIRONMENT` (viewport + route) here as the first
28:    * message so the server session seeds from it.
29:    */
30:   onOpen?: (transport: Transport) => void;
31:   /** Injectable socket factory (tests). */
32:   createSocket?: (url: string) => WebSocket;
33: }
34: 
35: const BASE_DELAY_MS = 500;
36: const MAX_DELAY_MS = 30000;
37: const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 30;
38: 
39: // Heartbeat (spec/OPCODE.md §Transport heartbeat): the client probes server
40: // liveness with META::PING every HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS. It treats the connection
41: // as dead when NO server batch of any kind (deltas, META::PONG) has arrived for
42: // HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_MS — a stalled-but-"open" socket never fires onclose, so the
43: // watchdog forces a close to trigger the reconnect flow (which re-sends the
44: // environment + requests a META::RESYNC). The PING also counts as inbound WS
45: // traffic, keeping the connection warm through proxies and idle-spin-down.
46: const HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS = 5000;
47: const HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000;
48: const WATCHDOG_CHECK_MS = 1000;
49: 
50: // Numeric readyState (the WebSocket global may be absent in test environments).
51: const WS_OPEN = 1;
52: 
53: export class Transport {
54:   private ws: WebSocket | null = null;
55:   private attempt = 0;
56:   private stopped = false;
57:   private readonly options: TransportOptions;
58:   private pingTimer: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null = null;
59:   private watchdogTimer: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null = null;
60:   private lastActivityAt = 0;
61:   /**
62:    * The sequence the next guest → host delta batch must carry, or `null` before
63:    * the first batch / after a gap or reconnect (re-baseline on the next batch).
64:    * See spec/OPCODE.md §Sequence gap detection.
65:    */
66:   private expectedSequence: number | null = null;
67: 
68:   constructor(options: TransportOptions) {
69:     this.options = options;
70:   }
71: 
72:   /** Connect and stay connected (auto-reconnect with exponential backoff). */
73:   start(): void {
74:     this.stopped = false;
75:     this.lastActivityAt = Date.now();
76:     this.startHeartbeat();
77:     this.connect();
78:   }
79: 
80:   /** Permanently close the socket and cancel reconnects. */
81:   stop(): void {
82:     this.stopped = true;
83:     this.stopHeartbeat();
84:     if (this.ws) {
85:       this.ws.onclose = null;
86:       this.ws.close();
87:       this.ws = null;
88:     }
89:   }
90: 
91:   get open(): boolean {
92:     return this.ws !== null && this.ws.readyState === WS_OPEN;
93:   }
94: 
95:   send(bytes: Uint8Array): void {
96:     if (!this.open) {
97:       return;
98:     }
99:     // Best-effort description (never drops the bytes, even if undecodable).
100:     try {
101:       const batch = parseBatch(bytes);

103:       log.debug("ws", "→ send detail", describeBatchDetail(batch));
104:     } catch {
105:       log.info("ws", "→ send", bytes.length, "bytes");
106:     }
107:     this.ws!.send(bytes);
108:   }
109: 
110:   /** Start the META::PING sender + the no-activity watchdog (one-shot, survives reconnects). */
111:   private startHeartbeat(): void {
112:     if (this.pingTimer || this.watchdogTimer) {
113:       return;
114:     }
115:     this.pingTimer = setInterval(() => {
116:       if (this.open) {
117:         this.send(encodePing());
118:       }
119:     }, HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS);
120:     this.watchdogTimer = setInterval(() => {
121:       if (!this.open) {
122:         return;
123:       }
124:       if (Date.now() - this.lastActivityAt > HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_MS) {
125:         log.warn("ws", `no server frame for ${HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_MS} ms — reconnecting`);
126:         this.ws?.close();
127:       }
128:     }, WATCHDOG_CHECK_MS);
129:   }
130: 
131:   private stopHeartbeat(): void {
132:     if (this.pingTimer) {
133:       clearInterval(this.pingTimer);
134:       this.pingTimer = null;
135:     }
136:     if (this.watchdogTimer) {
137:       clearInterval(this.watchdogTimer);
138:       this.watchdogTimer = null;
139:     }
140:   }
141: 
142:   private connect(): void {
143:     log.debug("ws", "connecting", this.options.url);
144:     const ws = this.options.createSocket
145:       ? this.options.createSocket(this.options.url)
146:       : new WebSocket(this.options.url);
147:     this.ws = ws;
148:     ws.binaryType = "arraybuffer";
149:     ws.onopen = () => {
150:       // A reconnect means the client missed deltas while disconnected: request a
151:       // full snapshot (META::RESYNC). The first connect never does — the client
152:       // already has the whole UI from the SSR HTML. On EVERY open (before any
153:       // resync) the client sends its environment (viewport + route).
154:       this.lastActivityAt = Date.now();
155:       // Re-baseline the sequence on the next guest → host batch (a fresh
156:       // connection's stream restarts; see §Sequence gap detection).
157:       this.expectedSequence = null;
158:       const reconnected = this.attempt > 0;
159:       this.attempt = 0;
160:       log.info("ws", reconnected ? "connected (reconnect)" : "connected");
161:       this.options.onStatus?.("open");
162:       this.options.onOpen?.(this);
163:       if (reconnected) {
164:         log.debug("ws", "requesting RESYNC (missed deltas while disconnected)");
165:         this.send(encodeResync());
166:       }
167:     };
168:     ws.onmessage = (event) => this.handleMessage(event.data);
169:     ws.onerror = () => {
170:       log.error("ws", "socket error");
171:       // onclose always follows; nothing to do here.
172:     };
173:     ws.onclose = () => {
174:       this.ws = null;
175:       if (this.stopped) {
176:         log.debug("ws", "closed (stopped)");
177:         return;
178:       }
179:       log.info("ws", "closed — reconnecting (attempt", this.attempt + 1 + ")");
180:       this.options.onStatus?.("reconnecting");
181:       this.scheduleReconnect();
182:     };
183:   }
184: 
185:   private scheduleReconnect(): void {
186:     if (this.attempt >= MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
187:       return;
188:     }
189:     const delay = Math.min(BASE_DELAY_MS * 2 ** this.attempt, MAX_DELAY_MS);
190:     this.attempt++;
191:     setTimeout(() => this.connect(), delay);
192:   }
193: 
194:   private handleMessage(data: unknown): void {
195:     // Any server batch (a delta, a META::PONG, anything) proves the connection
196:     // is alive — reset the heartbeat watchdog.
197:     this.lastActivityAt = Date.now();
198:     let bytes: Uint8Array;
199:     if (data instanceof ArrayBuffer) {
200:       bytes = new Uint8Array(data);
201:     } else if (data instanceof Blob) {
202:       void data.arrayBuffer().then((buffer) => this.handleMessage(buffer));
203:       return;
204:     } else {
205:       bytes = new Uint8Array(0);
206:     }
207:     let batch: Batch;
208:     try {
209:       batch = parseBatch(bytes);
210:     } catch (err) {
211:       if (err instanceof ProtocolError) {
212:         log.error("ws", "rejected batch:", err.message);
213:         return;
214:       }
215:       throw err;
216:     }
217:     log.info("ws", "← recv", describeBatch(batch));
218:     log.debug("ws", "← recv detail", describeBatchDetail(batch));
219:     if (batch.version !== VERSION) {
220:       log.warn("ws", `protocol version ${batch.version} != ${VERSION}; reloading`);
221:       location.reload();
222:       return;
223:     }
224:     // Sequence gap detection (spec/OPCODE.md §Sequence gap detection): a
225:     // guest → host delta batch whose sequence breaks the chain means one or more
226:     // batches were lost while the socket stayed open. Do not apply the gapped
227:     // batch (its deltas assume the lost state); request a full snapshot and
228:     // re-baseline on the next batch.
229:     if (this.isSequenceGap(batch)) {
230:       log.warn(
231:         "ws",
232:         `sequence gap: expected ${this.expectedSequence}, got ${batch.sequence} — requesting RESYNC`,
233:       );
234:       this.expectedSequence = null;
235:       this.send(encodeResync());
236:       return;
237:     }
238:     this.trackSequence(batch);
239:     try {
240:       applyBatch(batch, this.options.renderer);
241:     } catch (err) {
242:       if (err instanceof ProtocolError) {
243:         log.error("ws", "rejected delta:", err.message);
244:         return;
245:       }
246:       throw err;
247:     }
248:     this.options.onBatch?.(batch);
249:   }
250: 
251:   /**
252:    * True when a guest → host delta batch breaks the expected sequence chain.
253:    * Host → guest batches (heartbeat `PONG`, request echoes) carry sequence 0 and
254:    * are not part of the guest → host stream, so they are ignored here.
255:    */
256:   private isSequenceGap(batch: Batch): boolean {
257:     if ((batch.flags & FLAG_HOST_TO_GUEST) !== 0) {
258:       return false;
259:     }
260:     return this.expectedSequence !== null && batch.sequence !== this.expectedSequence;
261:   }
262: 
263:   /** Advance the expected sequence from a guest → host delta batch (baseline or next). */
264:   private trackSequence(batch: Batch): void {
265:     if ((batch.flags & FLAG_HOST_TO_GUEST) !== 0) {
266:       return;
267:     }
268:     this.expectedSequence = batch.sequence + 1;
269:   }
270: }

# @pathland/dom-renderer

The **Pathland DOM renderer** — the web client. A small, vanilla-TypeScript
hydration client (zero runtime dependencies) that:

- **Hydrates** the server-rendered DOM by `data-pathland-id`.
- **Decodes** self-contained `PLPL` opcode batches (bounds-checked) and applies
  them in place: **`STYLE` deltas** (the full property catalog — layout, text,
  styling, effects, semantic/control variants, plus `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` →
  CSS variables) and **`TREE` deltas** (create/delete/insert/remove/move —
  runtime structural updates without a full reload).
- **Reports raw inputs** back over WebSocket as `EVENT` batches — the full event
  catalog (pointer down/move/up, key down/up, value/text/date changed, focus/
  editing, submit, scroll, wheel) — guest → host (flags `0x0000`), gated by the
  SSR `EVENT_LISTENERS` mask.
- **Negotiates** the protocol version (mismatch → reload) and **reconnects**
  with exponential backoff.

Styling is **Option A**: the protocol stays renderer-agnostic; the SSR HTML
carries Tailwind classes (server-compiled), and runtime style deltas are applied
as inline style (overriding the current value), with literal colors inline and
semantic design tokens as CSS variables. The DOM renderer owns the bounded
property → style/class map (`src/classes.ts`).

## Layout

```
src/
  constants.ts   protocol constants (mirror spec/)
  plpl.ts        bounds-checked batch parse + string decode
  format.ts      f32/ARGB/date/float formatting
  elements.ts    component → DOM shell factory (TREE create)
  classes.ts     Option A style/state appliers (inline style + ARIA + CSS vars)
  apply.ts       delta application (STYLE + TREE) over the id → Node registry
  events.ts      guest → host EVENT encoders
  transport.ts   WebSocket connect/reconnect/version negotiation
  index.ts       bootstrap (hydrate + connect + listeners)
```

## Build & test

```bash
npm ci
npm test          # vitest (happy-dom): codec round-trips, TREE/STYLE apply, transport
npm run build     # tsc --noEmit + esbuild -> dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js (IIFE, minified)
npm run copy-to-demos   # copy the bundle into both Java demos' static dirs
```

## The bundle

`dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` is served by the Spring Boot and Quarkus demos under a
content-hashed name — `dom-renderer-<sha256>.js` (copied into each demo's static
resources by `npm run copy-to-demos`, which also prunes stale copies and writes the
`dom-renderer.current` pointer manifest the SSR layer reads to emit the `<script src>`).
The fresh URL per build busts the immutable asset cache.

## Transport resilience

`src/transport.ts` reconnects with exponential backoff, keeps the connection
alive with a `META::PING`/`PONG` heartbeat + no-activity watchdog, and recovers
from lost deltas: a **sequence gap** (a batch whose per-stream `sequence` breaks
the chain) makes the client skip the gapped batch and request a full snapshot
(`META::RESYNC`). See `spec/OPCODE.md` §Transport heartbeat and §Sequence gap
detection.

1: // Lazy web-icon glyph resolution. SSR inlines every rendered icon's `<path>`
2: // in the page, so first render is fully embedded — no network, no cache
3: // dependency. The DOM client only needs glyph data when a delta asks for an
4: // `ICON_NAME` that the page has *not* embedded. Instead of shipping the full
5: // canonical catalog in the bundle (~13KB), the glyph is resolved lazily:
6: //   1. the JS memo cache (this session),
7: //   2. an already-embedded `svg.pathland-icon[data-pathland-icon=name]`
8: //      elsewhere in the page — its inner markup, zero bytes and zero network,
9: //   3. the renderer-owned `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` the host serves from
10: //      the shared Rust library (`pathland_html_icon_svg` over the C ABI — the
11: //      same source SSR inlines from), fetched once then memoized + HTTP-cached.
12: // Unknown/extension names and fetch failures resolve to the fallback glyph.
13: 
14: const cache = new Map<string, string>();
15: const inflight = new Map<string, Promise<string>>();
16: const current = new WeakMap<Element, string>();
17: 
18: /** The reserved framework root (`/_pathland` by default; relocated via the SSR page's `data-pathland-base`). */
19: function basePath(): string {
20:   return document.documentElement.dataset.pathlandBase ?? "/_pathland";
21: }
22: 
23: /** The decorative fallback glyph (a faint circle) — the renderer's `web_fallback_svg()`. */
24: export const FALLBACK_SVG = '<circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8"/>';
25: 
26: /** The inner markup of an already-embedded icon svg for `name`, if present. */
27: function embeddedGlyph(name: string): string | undefined {
28:   for (const svg of document.querySelectorAll("svg.pathland-icon[data-pathland-icon]")) {
29:     if (svg.getAttribute("data-pathland-icon") === name) {
30:       return svg.innerHTML;
31:     }
32:   }
33:   return undefined;
34: }
35: 
36: /**
37:  * Memorize every glyph the page has embedded — the SSR inlines each rendered
38:  * icon, so a name that was ever on screen is capturable without a fetch. The
39:  * seeds are DOM-only, so without this the very element being swapped would be
40:  * the only play glyph and flipping it to pause would make the return trip to
41:  * play a (cached) fetch. Skips empty/shadowed contents (a mid-fill element).
42:  */
43: function harvestEmbedded(): void {
44:   for (const svg of document.querySelectorAll("svg.pathland-icon[data-pathland-icon]")) {
45:     const name = svg.getAttribute("data-pathland-icon");
46:     if (!name || cache.has(name)) continue;
47:     const glyph = svg.innerHTML.trim();
48:     if (glyph) cache.set(name, glyph);
49:   }
50: }
51: 
52: async function fetchGlyph(name: string): Promise<string> {
53:   try {
54:     const url = new URL(`${basePath()}/icons/${encodeURIComponent(name)}.svg`, document.baseURI);
55:     const res = await fetch(url.href);
56:     if (!res.ok) return FALLBACK_SVG;
57:     const text = (await res.text()).trim();
58:     // The served file is the same markup SSR inlines: `<svg …>…inner…</svg>`.
59:     const inner = text.slice(text.indexOf(">") + 1, text.lastIndexOf("</svg>"));
60:     return inner || FALLBACK_SVG;
61:   } catch {
62:     return FALLBACK_SVG;
63:   }
64: }
65: 
66: /**
67:  * Ensure a glyph is cached for `name` (resolves to it, or the fallback on
68:  * failure/unknown). Deduplicated: concurrent callers share one fetch.
69:  */
70: export function preloadIcon(name: string): Promise<string> {
71:   const existing = inflight.get(name);
72:   if (existing) return existing;
73:   const done = fetchGlyph(name).then((glyph) => {
74:     cache.set(name, glyph);
75:     inflight.delete(name);
76:     return glyph;
77:   });
78:   inflight.set(name, done);
79:   return done;
80: }
81: 
82: /**
83:  * Set/swap an icon node's glyph: memo cache → an embedded glyph (the element
84:  * itself, or a sibling) → the fallback now, then the fetched glyph when it
85:  * arrives (only if the element still shows `name`). All synchronous calls are
86:  * instant; the only async path is a name the page never embedded.
87:  */
88: export function setIcon(svg: Element, name: string): void {
89:   if (!svg) return;
90:   current.set(svg, name);
91:   if (!name) {
92:     svg.removeAttribute("data-pathland-icon");
93:     svg.innerHTML = FALLBACK_SVG;
94:     return;
95:   }
96:   // Resolve BEFORE mutating the element: `embeddedGlyph` scans the document
97:   // (which includes `svg` itself), so rewriting the element's
98:   // `data-pathland-icon` first would make it match its own OLD inner markup
99:   // (a hydrated play button would paste its play glyph back on a pause delta —
100:   // the icon would never change). Resolved against the current DOM, the
101:   // element still advertises the name it actually shows.
102:   const memo = cache.get(name);
103:   if (memo !== undefined) {
104:     svg.setAttribute("data-pathland-icon", name);
105:     svg.innerHTML = memo;
106:     return;
107:   }
108:   const embedded = embeddedGlyph(name);
109:   if (embedded !== undefined) {
110:     cache.set(name, embedded);
111:     svg.setAttribute("data-pathland-icon", name);
112:     svg.innerHTML = embedded;
113:     return;
114:   }
115:   // A miss: memorize every glyph the page has EMBEDDED (the SSR seeds are
116:   // DOM-only — the moment this element flips away from "play" its play glyph
117:   // would otherwise evaporate and the return trip would refetch it). One pass,
118:   // then re-check; a name that is still absent genuinely needs the lazy fetch.
119:   harvestEmbedded();
120:   const harvested = cache.get(name);
121:   if (harvested !== undefined) {
122:     svg.setAttribute("data-pathland-icon", name);
123:     svg.innerHTML = harvested;
124:     return;
125:   }
126:   svg.setAttribute("data-pathland-icon", name);
127:   svg.innerHTML = FALLBACK_SVG;
128:   void preloadIcon(name).then((glyph) => {
129:     if (current.get(svg) === name) svg.innerHTML = glyph;
130:   });
131: }

# @pathland/dom-renderer (lib/typescript) — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 1, 2026

The **Pathland DOM renderer** — the web client. A vanilla-TypeScript hydration
client (no runtime dependencies) that is the single source of the client,
replacing the two duplicated `app.js` files in the demos. Protocol contract:
`spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Single source, unified**: `src/` is the one client; `npm run build` emits
  `dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` (IIFE, minified via esbuild), and
  `npm run copy-to-demos` copies it into both the Quarkus and Spring Boot demos'
  static resource dirs under a **content-hashed name** (`dom-renderer-<sha256>.js`),
  pruning stale `dom-renderer-*.js` and the pre-hash literal `dom-renderer.js` (the old
  duplicated `app.js` is long since removed). A one-line pointer manifest
  `dom-renderer.current` sits next to the copies; the SSR layer reads it
  (`PathlandAssets`) to emit the right `<script src>` — the fresh URL per build busts
  the immutable asset cache without any hard refresh.

2: //
3: // A control with an active continuous-input session (a range slider being
4: // dragged) is authoritative for the state it edits: the DOM client must not

6: // cannot fight the pointer and cause flicker. At most one drag happens at a
7: // time, so a single active-range slot suffices.

10: 
11: /** Mark a range slider as being dragged (its thumb is user-authoritative). */
12: export function markRangeInFlight(el: HTMLInputElement): void {
13:   activeRange = el;

15: 
16: /** Clear the marker when a specific range is released/blurred. */
17: export function unmarkRangeInFlight(el: HTMLInputElement): void {
18:   if (activeRange === el) {
19:     activeRange = null;
20:   }
21: }
22:

24: export function clearInFlightRange(): void {
25:   activeRange = null;

6: // `documentElement.style` — an inline dark override would beat the media query
7: // and break light mode.
8: //
9: // The token *conventions* (`tokenToCssVar`, `isDarkToken`, `isLengthToken`,
10: // `resolveTokenCssRef` and the length-token tables) are generated from
11: // `pathland-render-html::token_spec` by `pathland-ts-codegen` — see
12: // `generated/tokens-core.ts`.
13: 
14: import type { Batch, Opcode } from "./plpl";
15: import { readString } from "./plpl";
16: import { VAL_COLOR, VAL_F32, VAL_I32, VAL_STRING, VAL_U8, VAL_U32 } from "./constants";
17: import { argbToRgba, f32FromBits } from "./format";
18: import {
19:   isDarkToken,
20:   isLengthToken,
21:   tokenToCssVar,
22: } from "./generated/tokens-core";
23: 
24: // Re-exported for callers that use the token conventions directly.
25: export { isDarkToken, resolveTokenCssRef, tokenToCssVar } from "./generated/tokens-core";
26: 
27: /** Render a token value as a CSS value string per the value type. */
28: export function tokenCssValue(valueType: number, c: number): string {
29:   switch (valueType) {
30:     case VAL_COLOR:
31:       return argbToRgba(c);
32:     case VAL_F32:
33:       return String(f32FromBits(c));
34:     case VAL_I32:
35:       return String(c | 0);
36:     case VAL_U32:
37:       return String(c >>> 0);
38:     case VAL_U8:
39:       return String(c & 0xff);
40:     default:
41:       return String(c >>> 0);
42:   }
43: }
44: 
45: /** Render a token override value as CSS, appending `px` to F32 length tokens.
46:  *  `STRING` values (e.g. `font.body.family`) are single-quoted and escaped. */
47: function tokenCssOverride(path: string, valueType: number, value: number | string): string {
48:   if (typeof value === "string") {
49:     return `'${value.replace(/\\/g, "\\\\").replace(/'/g, "\\'")}'`;
50:   }
51:   const v = tokenCssValue(valueType, value);
52:   return isLengthToken(path) && valueType === VAL_F32 ? v + "px" : v;
53: }
54: 
55: export interface DesignTokenSink {
56:   setToken(path: string, valueType: number, value: number | string): void;
57: }
58: 
59: /**
60:  * Applies token overrides to a managed `<style data-pathland-tokens>` element:
61:  * base tokens as `:root` rules, `dark.*` tokens inside
62:  * `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`. The element is appended to `<head>`
63:  * after the SSR built-in style block, so equal-specificity rules win in order.
64:  */
65: export function createTokenSink(): DesignTokenSink {
66:   const base = new Map<string, string>();
67:   const dark = new Map<string, string>();
68:   let styleEl: HTMLStyleElement | null = null;
69: 
70:   function render(): void {
71:     const rules: string[] = [];
72:     for (const [name, value] of base) {
73:       rules.push(`:root{${name}:${value};}`);
74:     }
75:     if (dark.size > 0) {
76:       const darkRules: string[] = [];
77:       for (const [name, value] of dark) {
78:         darkRules.push(`:root{${name}:${value};}`);
79:       }
80:       rules.push(`@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark){${darkRules.join("")}}`);
81:     }
82:     if (!styleEl) {
83:       styleEl = document.createElement("style");
84:       styleEl.setAttribute("data-pathland-tokens", "");
85:       document.head.appendChild(styleEl);
86:     }
87:     styleEl.textContent = rules.join("");
88:   }
89: 
90:   return {
91:     setToken(path, valueType, value) {
92:       const name = tokenToCssVar(path);
93:       const cssValue = tokenCssOverride(path, valueType, value);
94:       (isDarkToken(path) ? dark : base).set(name, cssValue);
95:       render();
96:     },
97:   };
98: }
99: 
100: /**
101:  * Handle a PARAMETER `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` opcode (spec/OPCODE.md design-token system):
102:  * `A = arenaRef (token path)`, `B = valueType (u8, low byte)`, `C = value`. For
103:  * a `STRING` value type, `C` is an arenaRef to the value string, resolved here.
104:  */
105: export function applyDesignToken(op: Opcode, strings: Uint8Array, sink: DesignTokenSink): void {
106:   const path = readString(strings, op.a);
107:   const valueType = op.b & 0xff;
108:   const value: number | string = valueType === VAL_STRING ? readString(strings, op.c) : op.c;
109:   sink.setToken(path, valueType, value);
110: }
111: 
112: /** Convenience: apply every SET_DESIGN_TOKEN opcode in a batch. */
113: export function applyDesignTokens(batch: Batch, sink: DesignTokenSink): void {
114:   for (const op of batch.opcodes) {
115:     if (op.category === 0x02 /* STYLE */ && op.command === 0x02 /* SET_DESIGN_TOKEN */) {
116:       applyDesignToken(op, batch.strings, sink);
117:     }
118:   }
119: }
